purpose.summary: Close the two deferred reconstruction canaries for the bounded Chronik projection using only public functional tests and documentation.
scope: Ask two falsifiable questions without changing production code: does -reindex-chainstate replay the exact height-288 active chain into the projection, and can normal startup reconstruct the exact retained suffix after old block bodies have truly been pruned?

For -reindex-chainstate, bind the pre-restart active tip and UTXO-set hash, require an empty observer bootstrap, exclude full block-file reindexing, and verify 289 exact ordered connects from genesis through height 288.

For pruning, create only enough large regtest blocks whose coinbase claims zero value to cross one 128 MiB block-file boundary, advance cheaply to height 1001, manually prune through height 713, and require physical removal of blk00000.dat.
Prove that the pruned block body at height 1 is unavailable while its header remains readable and that retained height 714 plus tip 1001 remain readable.

Restart the explicit local-regtest observer on the same pruned datadir, require atomic reconstruction of exactly heights 714 through 1001 with 288 blocks and transactions, then mine height 1002 while keeping the 288-entry bound.
Keep all existing compiled-out, compiled-in-disabled, local-regtest-only, observe/index-only, and no-consensus-authority boundaries unchanged.
exclusions: No production, C++, Rust, CMake, consensus, chain-parameter, activation, testnet, mainnet, P2P, RPC, wallet, or user-interface code changes.
No persistent index, database, format, migration, resume marker, API, socket, service, or thread is added.
No automatic-pruning policy, multi-file pruning matrix, corrupt block file, abrupt crash, or power-loss behavior is claimed.
No mempool reconstruction, SLP, ALP, CashTokens classification, authoritative token state, native-asset validation, or governed consensus activation is added or demonstrated.
No local binary, build cache, raw output, absolute host path, parent environment, operator material, private history, or unrelated product material enters this change.

files.production_reachability: None; public test-boundary and operator documentation only.
files.test_reachability: Documents the distinct chainstate-reindex and actually-pruned reconstruction canaries, their exact retained suffix, and bounded temporary disk cost.

Adds a fresh -reindex-chainstate process at height 288 and compares active tip, UTXO-set hash, 289 ordered callbacks, projection totals, absence of block-file reindexing, and the inherited deep-reorg recovery path.
Creates a fresh manual-pruning regtest datadir, proves physical old-block removal, restarts the observer on exactly the readable 288-block suffix, and checks the next bounded connect.

Adds an optional coinbase-value input to the existing large-block helper so the new pruning canary can generate consensus-valid Ergon blocks whose coinbase claims zero value; the default behavior is unchanged.

commands: Build the exact public candidate with both Chronik options OFF and run the inherited legacy mining smoke.
expected_results: No Chronik source, option, object, symbol, or link edge enters bitcoind; legacy mining remains unchanged.

commands: Build with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON, leave runtime opt-in absent, and run the inherited legacy mining smoke.
expected_results: The observer library is linked but no observer is registered and no Chronik state, path, or socket exists; legacy mining remains unchanged.

commands: Run feature_chronik_block_observer.py and feature_chronik_pruned_observer.py with --hermetic-child-env against the compiled-in build, each on its own fresh isolated datadir.
expected_results: All six governed reconstruction scenarios pass without production changes, persistence, API state, native-asset behavior, or consensus authority.

scenarios.command: Run the inherited disabled then explicit local-regtest observer boundary in feature_chronik_block_observer.py.
expected_results: Disabled execution remains inert; exact local-regtest opt-in observes canonical blocks; non-regtest profiles reject the flag; no Chronik path or socket exists.
failure_conditions: Any disabled state, enabled non-regtest launch, callback mismatch, Chronik path/socket, validation decision, or activation claim fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run the inherited height-288 normal-restart recovery in feature_chronik_block_observer.py.
expected_results: A fresh process reconstructs exactly the readable 288-block suffix and keeps the same bound after the next connect.
failure_conditions: Partial adoption, wrong suffix or totals, stale rebuild-required state, or growth beyond 288 fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run the inherited full -reindex process on the existing active chain at height 288.
expected_results: The observer starts empty, receives exact ordered connects from genesis through height 288, and retains only the most recent 288 entries.
failure_conditions: Missing, duplicated, reordered, or rejected callbacks; prior-state reuse; incorrect hashes, payloads, totals, or bound fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: After the full-reindex canary reaches height 288, record tip and UTXO-set hash, stop, then start a fresh observer process with -reindex-chainstate=1.
expected_results: Bootstrap is empty; no block-file reindex occurs; tip and UTXO-set hash are unchanged; exact connects 0 through 288 rebuild the same bounded projection; no disconnect, rejection, or rebuild-required state occurs.
failure_conditions: A non-empty bootstrap masking replay, block-file reindex, changed tip or UTXO hash, callback divergence, rejection, or incomplete projection fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: On a separate fresh manual-pruning regtest datadir, cross one block-file boundary, reach height 1001, prune through 713, prove old-body removal, then restart with explicit observer opt-in.
expected_results: blk00000.dat is absent; height-1 block data is unavailable while its header remains; heights 714 and 1001 remain readable; bootstrap adopts exactly 714 through 1001 with 288 blocks and transactions; height 1002 keeps the bound.
failure_conditions: No physical file removal, readable old body, unreadable retained body, bootstrap outside 714 through 1001, minted bootstrap event, incorrect totals, or bound growth fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Continue the inherited deep reorganization after the new chainstate-reindex process at height 288, then reconsider and restart.
expected_results: Exactly 288 LIFO disconnects end at sequence 577; one rebuild-required transition rejects reconsidered events; normal restart reconstructs the active suffix.
failure_conditions: Mutation after rebuild-required, non-LIFO acceptance, silent continuation past the anchor, node consensus influence, or restart recovery failure fails the scenario.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public verification after technical acceptance

limitations: This change modifies only functional tests and documentation; it adds no production capability beyond the already-published bounded volatile projection.
The pruning canary covers one manually pruned block file on regtest; it does not cover automatic pruning, multiple removed files, corrupt files, abrupt termination, or power loss.
The large-block helper's new coinbase-value parameter is exercised with zero for Ergon; its inherited default behavior is unchanged but the full historical 4 GiB pruning suite is not rerun locally.

The new pruning canary is auto-selected in the default functional-test set when the observer component is compiled; its intended peak is below 250 MiB, but public verification must record actual duration and disk use.
The observer remains volatile and non-queryable; none of these recovery canaries demonstrates durable index state, crash-safe persistence, or API compatibility.
The local run reuses the exact published 0028 production binary because this change has no build or production source postimage; public verification must rebuild the exact candidate tree.
Functional tests are not claimed on Windows, where this inherited test system disables them by default.
Local tests are contradiction checks only; no result is public reproduction evidence at record-review time.
counterevidence: No public build or functional execution of the exact candidate exists at record-review time.
A single manual-pruning regtest case is not evidence for automatic production pruning policy, arbitrary disk layouts, corrupted storage, or crash recovery.
Successful reconstruction from public block inputs does not demonstrate persistence, mempool reconstruction, SLP/ALP/CashTokens recognition, token validity, consensus rules, or activation behavior.
The unchanged default path remains the authority: Chronik is compiled out or runtime disabled unless explicitly enabled on local regtest.
